case_title: Rajib Ranjan & Ors. v. R. Vijaykumar
accused_occupation: Public servants (Gazetted officers of the Chhattisgarh State Government, as contended by appellants; High Court accepted they are public servants)
accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute in a tender process: the complainant was a rejected bidder; the accused were officials involved in the tender rejection, and a competing bidder was also an accused
evidence_type: Documentary: tender records, JSEB performance information, General Manager's report, technical experts' report
trial_court_outcome: Took cognizance of the complaint and issued summons to the appellants (pre-trial; no verdict or sentence)
high_court_outcome: Petitions under s.482 CrPC seeking quashing dismissed; High Court held s.197 not attracted
neutral_facts: The victim's company submitted a bid in response to a state electricity board tender for the design, supply and erection of an ignition system at a thermal power station. The bid was returned without being opened after the tender committee found that the bidder had not furnished a required performance report, despite repeated requests and an assurance to supply it. The board sought performance information from another state electricity board. An official deputed to obtain it reported that the bidder's earlier works were unsatisfactory. The general manager of that other power station reported defects in a scanning system supplied by the bidder, which had adversely affected generation. Technical experts also opined that the bidder was not technically suitable on technical vetting and comparative data. The victim alleged that the accused, together with the successful bidder and another official, conspired to fabricate a performance report cum certificate dated 28 December 2004. The victim alleged the certificate was false, malafide and defamatory, that it was designed to discredit the victim's company and favour the successful bidder, and that it caused the loss of a chance to obtain a contract. The documents available were the tender records, the performance information, the general manager's report and the expert report.
financial_property_loss: No money or property quantified; alleged loss of a contract opportunity (Boiler Plant Units, Korba)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Court; planning and conspiracy to fabricate the certificate was only alleged by the complainant
motive: Court's view of complainant's motive: to give criminal colour to a civil dispute over the rejected tender (alleged motive of complainant; Court did not accept the fabrication allegation)
key_evidence_accepted: Tender committee's pre-qualification rejection, the JSEB officer's report, the General Manager's report of 28.12.2004 on scanning system defects, and the technical experts' opinion; Court held the tender rejection was in discharge of official duties
witness_credibility: No witness credibility assessed; Court found the complainant's forgery allegations an afterthought and not bona fide
trial_duration: offence: not given (alleged certificate dated 28.12.2004); trial judgment: not given (cognizance order date not stated); High Court: 03.06.2009; Supreme Court: 14.10.2014
legal_representation: Appellants: Rahul Srivastava, Ram Swarup Sharma. Respondent (complainant) appeared in person. State counsel not stated.
investigation_status: Police declined to register the complaint as a civil dispute; private complaint filed before the Magistrate, registered as C.C. No. 183/07, and cognizance taken
appeal_history: Trial court (Judicial Magistrate): cognizance taken and summons issued. High Court: quashing petitions dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, summoning orders set aside, complaint dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Complainant argued the accused conspired and created a false document to reject his claim; sanction under s.197 not required as the charges were conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust and defamation; complainant's legal status was accepted by the Magistrate
defence_argument: Appellants argued that s.197 sanction was mandatory, the complaint disclosed no offence, the complainant lacked locus standi as CEI was not a registered company, and the complaint was an abuse of process after civil remedies failed
legal_principle_applied: Sanction under s.197 CrPC arises only for acts in discharge of official duty, not for criminal conspiracy or fabrication; quashing under s.482 CrPC where proceedings are mala fide, an abuse of process, or convert a civil dispute into a criminal case (Bhajan Lal principles 6 and 7)
precedent_relied_upon: Shambhoo Nath Misra v. State of U.P. (1997) 5 SCC 326; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335; Indian Oil Corpn. v. NEPC India Ltd. (2006) 6 SCC 736; Inder Mohan Goswami v. State of Uttaranchal (2007) 12 SCC 1; also State of Maharashtra v. Dr. Budhikota Subbarao (1993) 2 SCC 567 and G. Sagar Suri (2000) 2 SCC 636 as quoted
other_sentence_order: Complaint dismissed; cognizance and summoning orders set aside; no order as to costs
